question_text: Attach your government operations emissions inventory and report the following information regarding this inventory.
col4_Boundary: Departments, entities or companies over which operational control is exercised
col6_Primary protocol: Local Government Operations Protocol (ICLEI USA, The Climate Registry, California Climate Action Registry, California Air Resources Board)
col7_Emissions sources included: Subway / underground|Municipal vehicle fleet|Maritime port|Thermal energy|Buses|Buildings|Street lighting and traffic signals|Airport(s)|Wastewater treatment
col9_Comment: San Francisco began reporting department level GHG emissions in Fiscal Year 2008-2009. We track emissions generated from stationary and mobile combustion, electricity, and steam purchases. Beginning in FY 2011-2012, SF also reported estimated wastewater emissions. The city reports on a limited set of scope 3 emissions: fugitive emissions related to natural gas distribution (upstream and downstream), and electricity transmission and distribution loss emissions. Electricity for municipal buildings and operations is provided primarily by the Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC) and comes from our municipally-owned and operated hydro-electric dam at Hetch Hetchy. Natural gas is provided by Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E) but billed through SFPUC. Data is obtained primarily from SFPUC Power and Water, GSA Fleet Management - Central Shops, the Real Estate Division, the Municipal Transportation Agency and PG&E. Additional data is collected from departments that obtain vehicle fuel or building energy outside of these sources. These departments include Recreation and Parks, the Port, the airport (SFO), and others. Data from all sources are consolidated into a database. Each year, the Environment Department (SFE) presents energy, vehicle fuel and water use data, along with associated GHG emissions, for each department via a dashboard. Energy data is broken out by electricity, natural gas and steam. Fuel data is broken out into diesel, biodiesel, gasoline, LPG, and CNG. Department climate liaisons review and verify the data, and notify SFE and relevant departments, if corrections need to be made. There are over 70 climate liaisons who work with fleet managers, facility engineers and managers, etc., to supply and verify data. Emissions are calculated per LGOP guidelines and emission factors for each dept. The GHG emissions for each dept are added together to obtain the total for the City and County of San Francisco (CCSF). Starting inventory year 2015, the emissions from this municipal operations inventory is a subset of and is thus aggregated into community-wide emissions. This allowed CCSF to align communications of municipal and community-wide emissions. Public Transportation from city owned/operated buses and light-rail run by the SFMTA (aka MUNI) is also included in this municipal inventory. Emissions from MUNI's bus and light rail are reflected and broken out when aggregated into community-wide emissions under the Public Transportation subsector.
